text.p: Dutch publisher NV Verenigd Bezit VNU reaped the benefits of having a spread of businesses on Tuesday when it announced a 16 percent increase in net profit from ordinary operations for 1996.
VNU -- whose businesses span consumer magazines, business information and commercial TV -- also said it expected net profit and ordinary earnings to be higher this year.
The result was in line with expectations but analysts were cheered by the increasing contribution from its growing business information operations.
"My first reaction is that I am very positive about the result and its quality," said Generale Bank analyst Ab Barneveld.
However, VNU shares slipped roughly in line with the Amsterdam share market to stand at 40.60 guilders at 1050 GMT, down 30 cents from Monday's close.
VNU said 1996 net profit from ordinary operations rose 16 percent to 316 million guilders ($166.1 million) from 274 million in 1995.
The dividend rises to 0.55 guilders per share from 0.48 guilders in 1995.

Overall net profit, including extraordinary items, fell to 322 million guilders from 430 million in 1995 when it was swollen by an extraordinary gain of 157 million guilders on the sale of U.S. financial information unit Disclosure.

VNU said it expected a "clear" increase in earnings this year from consumer magazines, educational publishing and Business Information Europe plus a "significant" rise in earnings from newspapers and Business Information USA.
It said market conditions for commercial television remained "uncertain" but that it expected "some improvement" in results this year after a one million guilder loss in 1996.

In terms of operating profit, the European and U.S. business information divisions rose more than 40 percent and consumer magazines 17 percent, while newspapers gained one percent and commercial television made a loss due to tougher competition.
In consumer magazines, VNU said subscription and advertising revenues rose and leading market positions were maintained in the Netherlands and better results were achieved in Belgium and Britain.
Newspaper profits were below expectations due to higher paper costs, the launch of regional television and one-off costs for mergers of different newspaper titles.
Business Information Europe saw strong growth from the job advertisements market, while trade magazines in Britain and Belgium offset negative results in Italy.
VNU said VNU Marketing Information Services and BPI Communications were contributors to the substantial jump in profits from Business Information USA.
Andre Moons of ING Barings hailed the profit increases from business information of more than 40 percent in Europe and the United States.
"I regard that as very positive because the mix of sales is increasingly shifting to business-to-business," he said.
